ai.description: This 25–35 mm frog is brown with a dark, hourglass-shaped dorsal pattern. It features a pointed snout, a distinct dark lateral stripe, and extensively webbed toes. It belongs to the family Microhylidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Microhyla berdmorei* is best distinguished by its significantly expanded, heart-shaped toe discs, which are much larger than those of other Indian *Microhyla* species.
ai.habitat: *Microhyla berdmorei* inhabits moist evergreen and deciduous forests, typically found near streams or pools at elevations ranging from sea level to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Pegu Rice Frog is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by leaping into water to hide among submerged vegetation when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Microhyla berdmorei* breeds during the monsoon (May–August) in temporary pools, laying 300–500 eggs in a surface film. It is an explosive breeder with aquatic larvae.
ai.distributionRemarks: In the Indian subcontinent, *Microhyla berdmorei* inhabits the Northeast region, primarily across Assam, Meghalaya, and Mizoram, from lowlands up to 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Pegu Rice Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like buzzing trill. It is commonly heard calling from shallow, temporary rain pools in forest or agricultural habitats.
